title: How an invoice adds up
description: From a logged hour to the total on the invoice

steps.title: Client sets the rate
steps.explanation:
## Where the money starts

Every invoice belongs to one **client**, and the client carries the `hourly_rate`. Nothing else in the model knows a price.

steps.title: Hours times rate
steps.explanation:
A `LineItem` copies the rate when it is created, so changing a client's rate later never rewrites old invoices.

`total` rounds to cents here, once per line.

steps.title: Adding work
steps.explanation:
Two things are decided here, and the second is the one that matters.

`add` takes **hours only**: the rate always comes from the invoice's client, so a caller cannot bill one line at a different price by mistake. And the item is appended to the invoice it was added to, not to whichever invoice is current — there is no hidden state to get wrong.

The subtotal is a plain sum of the line totals; tax is computed on that sum, never per line.

steps.title: Tax and the total
steps.explanation: Tax is a rate applied to the subtotal and rounded to cents. The total is subtotal plus tax — nothing more.

steps.title: Showing it
steps.explanation: `invoicing list` prints one row per invoice, with its total and whether it is paid.
